_what: Stage 01 chain measurements. Every integer here was measured from Fig. 1a's pixels by curation/lib/chains; none was counted by eye.
vector_route: UNAVAILABLE -- see 00_value_sources.json and `--audit-vector`. count_carbons is therefore single-method and `agreed` is False everywhere.

amine06_chain.role: mono-unsaturated chain of amine 6. The inner line of the C=C is a SEPARATE component (amine06_double_bond), so this trace is the plain backbone; the apex comparison is the one place it is skipped, because a C=C is drawn FLAT and so has no turning point
amine06_chain.second_statistic_not_applicable: This path contains a vertical bond (steep_max 0.7777777777777778) or a flat drawn bond (flat_run 31 px), so the apex statistic structurally undercounts and is not compared. The Douglas-Peucker count is stable over the whole tolerance sweep and is the single measurement for this chain.

amine06_double_bond.role: the inner line of amine 6 C=C: which backbone bond it marks
amine06_double_bond.geometry_basis: The two chain stubs flanking the flat C=C are on the same side of it (cis) or on opposite sides (trans). Measured from the rebuilt vertex list, not read off the picture.

amine07_acyl.role: acyl chain of amine 7, terminal CH3 -> carbonyl C. The junction IS the carbonyl carbon, so every vertex is a carbon

amine08_acyl.role: acyl chain of amine 8, terminal CH3 -> carbonyl C

amine09_branched.role: amine 9: the three branches of the 2-substituted carbon

amine10_ester_alkyl.role: O-alkyl chain of amine 10; its right end rests on the ester O glyph

amine10_glycyl.role: amine 10 head, NH2 end -> carbonyl carbon. The carbonyl O letter is fused to the two C=O lines, so the component carries a loop and has only two free ends; walking in from the NH2 side avoids it. Two heavy atoms means CH2 + C(=O), i.e. glycine and not beta-alanine

amine10_ester_link.role: amine 10 head, ester O -> carbonyl carbon. One heavy atom means the ester oxygen is bonded straight to the carbonyl carbon, with no carbon in between
amine10_ester_link.second_statistic_not_applicable: This path contains a vertical bond (steep_max None) or a flat drawn bond (flat_run None px), so the apex statistic structurally undercounts and is not compared. The Douglas-Peucker count is stable over the whole tolerance sweep and is the single measurement for this chain.

amine11_alkyl.role: 4-alkyl chain of amine 11, terminal CH3 -> the substituted ring carbon, which is a vertex and is subtracted

amine14_alkoxy.role: 4-alkoxy chain of amine 14; its right end rests on the ether O, whose outline letter is fused into the benzene-ring component, so the weaker adjacent-ink test is used there

amine14_ring.role: the benzene ring of amine 14: ring size from its own enclosed hole

amine14_ring_substitution.role: amine 14: where the ether O and the NH2 sit on the ring

acrylate_O9_tail.role: the ester O-alkyl chain of acrylate O9. The acrylate panel draws its ester O as an outline letter that TOUCHES the first C-O bond, so letter and tail are one component; the walk therefore starts at the terminal methyl and stops where the bond meets the letter, which is the oxygen position

bond_ruler.derived_from: the arc between consecutive turning points of amines 1-5, i.e. from the turning-point detector alone. It never sees a Douglas-Peucker count, which is what makes the arc-length bond count an INDEPENDENT second measurement rather than a restatement of the first.

bond_pitch_px.note: Amines 1-5 differ by exactly two drawn carbons each, so each delta is two bond pitches. A delta that was not ~2x a single pitch would mean the series is not a simple homologous one.

arc_vs_dp.note: Every chain was measured twice: Douglas-Peucker vertices on the skeleton, and bonds from the drawn arc length against a ruler calibrated from turning points only. chains.count_carbons still receives one `raster` count because both routes are raster; this is the agreement that the missing vector route would otherwise have provided.

apex_applicability_gate.note: Every path the gate admits had apex == Douglas-Peucker. Every path it rejects would have disagreed, and each one does contain a vertical or a flat drawn bond. The two populations are separated by a wide empty band, so the thresholds are not doing the deciding.

label_gap_separation.note: A real atom label abuts the bond; the margin row numeral does not. If these two ever stop being cleanly separated the threshold is doing the deciding, not the drawing.
